card.title: How To Program ROM Chip for iPads with CD3217

source.title: How To Program ROM Chip for iPads with CD3217

claims.statement: iPads with the CD3217 USB-C controller that sit at 5 V instead of negotiating 15 V often have both the CD3217 and its adjacent ACE ROM damaged; a new CD3217 alone won't work.
The CD3217 and ROM are not paired, but the ROM holds firmware the CD3217 needs; fit a new CD3217 plus a ROM programmed from JC V1S Pro server files or a same-model donor dump.
A Wylie SPI programmer is a cheaper alternative to the JCID tool for writing the ROM.

procedure: Check negotiation on a USB-C meter (5 V = fault).
Inspect for corrosion/burn around CD3217 and ROM.
Program a blank ACE SPI flash (JC V1S Pro server file or donor dump).
Fit new CD3217 and programmed ROM; verify 15 V charging.
tools: JC V1S Pro with ROM module
card.caveats: Contradicts the separate iPad Pro 11 4th Gen page on whether CD3217 and ROM are 'paired'; both agree the ROM must come with or be programmed for the new chip. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
